task_description: A web-research QA task: find the book with DOI 10.2307/j.ctv9b2xdv (Noam Chomsky et al., 'The Responsibility of Intellectuals', UCL Press 2019), open page 11, locate the second-to-last paragraph, follow its endnote, and report the day-of-month in November on which a cited Wikipedia article was accessed. The gold answer is the single integer 4 (i.e., the Wikipedia citation in that endnote says it was accessed on 4 November). Success requires extracting the literal text of one endnote from inside the page-11 PDF.
final_vs_expected: produced None (run hit the 900s/30-msg cap with no FINAL ANSWER) vs gold 4 — the team never emitted any candidate, let alone the correct day.
primary_cause: The selector re-routed to WebResearcher on every one of the 6 turns and WebResearcher could never extract the page-11 endnote text from the JSTOR PDF (fetch_url returned raw binary), so the run looped on a single capability-blocked agent until timeout without ever reaching Analyst or Finalizer.
mast_rationale: 1.5 (unaware of termination conditions): there is a Finalizer role to emit 'FINAL ANSWER' but the selector never routed to it and WebResearcher never proposed any answer to finalize, so the run could only end by hitting the message cap — the system had no working path to stop. 1.3 (step repetition): WebResearcher repeats the same failing approach across all 6 turns — it re-fetches the identical JSTOR PDF URL (round 2 and round 4 of turn 1 fetch the exact same URL with identical truncated binary results) and re-runs near-identical 'j.ctv9b2xdv.11 Wikipedia accessed November' searches in turns 1,2,3,6 with no new strategy. 3.1 is borderline — really a non-termination/timeout rather than premature stop — included because the run terminated (by cap) with the task unsolved; the deeper issue is structural non-convergence, not genuine verification failure (3.2/3.3 do not apply: no answer was ever verified or accepted).
trace_narrative: Turn 1: selector opens with generic 'starting research' boilerplate and picks WebResearcher, which runs a 9-round private loop: it correctly resolves the DOI to 'The Responsibility of Intellectuals' (UCL Press, 2019) via Crossref, finds the page-11 chapter PDF (jstor.org/content/pdf/oa_chapter_edited/j.ctv9b2xdv.11, chapter 4 'The propaganda model and the British nuclear weapons debate' by Milan Rai), and twice fetches that PDF — but fetch_url returns only raw '%PDF-1.6' binary headers, not readable page text. It publishes an honest 'I couldn't verify the day' with the two source URLs. Turn 2: selector again picks WebResearcher; it privately muses about inferring from 'November 11, 2021' snippets, fetches the UCL discovery PDF (also raw binary), narrows to the right chapter, but publishes 'I couldn't verify the day of the month from the accessible sources.' Turn 3: WebResearcher hypothesizes the endnote cites the 'Nuclear weapons of the United Kingdom' Wikipedia article and searches for its access date; finds nothing usable; privately floats 'November 19, 2018' but again declines to guess and publishes the same can't-verify line. Turns 4 and 5: selector keeps re-selecting WebResearcher; each does a single trivial round and republishes the identical can't-verify message. Turn 6: WebResearcher runs two more rounds, gets a thin snippet, and publishes a final 'I couldn't verify... so I can't give a reliable number' with source URLs. The run then hits the 900s cap with no FINAL ANSWER. Only WebResearcher ever spoke; Analyst, Critic, and Finalizer were never selected.
open_ended_diagnosis: This is a structural non-convergence + single-agent capability failure, NOT inter-agent misalignment — and there is essentially no inter-agent dimension to misalign because only one of four roles ever acted. The root mechanical failure is tool capability: the answer lives in the rendered text of page 11 of the JSTOR PDF, but fetch_url returns raw, truncated PDF bytes ('%PDF-1.6 / endobj / stream …[truncated]') that contain no extractable endnote. WebResearcher correctly diagnosed this itself ('searching within the fetched PDF text isn't straightforward due to character limits', 'fetch_url could help me get the OCR text... but it seems truncated') yet had no tool to OCR/parse the PDF — that capability (run_python) belongs to Analyst, whom the selector never invoked. The second, compounding failure is the selector: facing a WebResearcher that had explicitly reported it could not retrieve the page text, the selector re-picked WebResearcher six straight times. Its turn-4 reasoning even names the alternative ('a critic might be useful... I wonder if I need more web research') and then routes back to WebResearcher anyway; it never considers Analyst (who could parse the PDF bytes with python) and never routes to Finalizer (so the run cannot terminate cleanly). The result is a one-agent loop that exhausts the budget. To WebResearcher's credit, it behaved honestly: privately it floated several candidate days (Nov 11, Nov 19) but consistently refused to publish a guess, so there is no fabrication and no verification theater. The team simply had no working path from 'PDF text is unreachable with my tool' to 'use a different tool/agent that can read it.'
reasoning_vs_published: There is NO meaningful private-vs-published divergence here — WebResearcher's published messages faithfully mirror its private state, which is the opposite of info-distortion (2.4). Privately it knew the real blocker: 'searching within the fetched PDF text isn't straightforward due to character limits' and 'I'll focus on searching within the PDF for terms like "Wikipedia"... fetch URL could help me get the OCR text for page 11' — and it published exactly that limitation: 'page 11 is in the JSTOR PDF, but the page text/endnote with the Wikipedia access date wasn't retrievable from the sources I could read.' Where it privately entertained guesses ('inferring it from a source accessed on November 11, 2021', 'inferred... it was accessed on November 19, 2018'), it correctly self-corrected ('I shouldn't guess though since I don't have direct information'; 'I'm realizing that I can't confirm this without further evidence') and withheld the guess from the team — honest reticence, not distortion. The only reasoning-vs-action gap that matters is the SELECTOR's: its turn-4 reasoning explicitly weighs a different role ('a critic might be useful, but I don't have a proposed answer right now') and its turn-5/6 reasoning concedes 'the web research tool didn't succeed' / 'the web researcher had some issues' — yet every time the action is to re-select WebResearcher. That is a reasoning-action mismatch at the selector level driving the structural loop, but it is misrouting/orchestration, not inter-agent misalignment among the worker agents (there was only one worker).
